note: A test file listed in docs/harness/ARCHAEOLOGY.md, or one test function in it (path = file::test_name), may be deleted only with an entry here: path, lesson, replacement (file::test_name that now carries the lesson), commit, date. tests/test_retirement_ledger.py enforces it. Empty on 2026-09-03: the archaeology found nothing to retire.

retired.lesson: Escalating is a write. The test asserted called == [] on a malformed triage result, so the fixed escalation (inbound:unknown + needs-human, dequeue) was planned and discarded and the item re-triaged every 15 minutes (#670). The rule it meant to encode, that the MODEL'S classification never reaches gh, is kept; the escalation carries nothing the model said and is written to the issue the workflow named.

A gap test is written to FAIL when its defect is fixed, and this one did: `macro_definition` is in the grammar and matched, and the extractor read the name with `_direct_name` (first DIRECT identifier child) while a macro's name sits at `signature > call_expression > identifier` (#748). The lesson it carried -- that a name helper looking one level too shallow drops the form in silence, with no ghost and no unmatched node type to find -- is kept and widened: the replacement asserts the macro extracts across four argument spellings AND that a macro and a function are named by the SAME path, which is why the fix reuses `_func_name` instead of adding a fifth bespoke helper.

The same lifecycle, one node type over: `_struct_name` read `type_head > identifier`, which is only the bare spelling, so seven of nine Julia type shapes yielded nothing while the two that worked were the least common in real code (#749). The lesson is that a fixture holding only the shapes that work reports a healthy language -- it was not wrong, it was narrow -- and it is kept by a replacement that parametrizes all nine shapes. The gap test's OTHER half, that a deeper walk must not fabricate symbols, is kept by two new rows asserting a supertype and a type parameter are not indexed as declarations.
